analysis: Examined the ProviderLoop+Capacity.swift diff (base vs head) and the one-line ProviderLoop+EngineV2.swift patch. Changes: (1) capacityRefreshTick now calls superviseTransitions() before the capacity rebuild (head line 62). Its body is not supplied, so its effects are unverified. (2) reclaimableMlx (head lines 174-175) now subtracts autopilotHeldWeightBytes(), clamped with min(mlxUsed, ...) so there is no underflow. This lowers the free_for_load_gb credit the provider advertises to the coordinator, so it is more conservative and cannot overstate capacity. It affects only routing and load-admission telemetry, not prompts, keys, attestation or the prefix cache (T-041 is not touched). (3) resliceGateGeneration &+= 1 in EngineV2 (wrapping increment, line 305) is a generation counter on the reslice gate. Wrapping arithmetic means no trap. The consumers of this counter are not in the supplied evidence. No authorization, encryption, attestation, key custody, or coordinator-wire changes were observed. The capacity payload shape is unchanged. Remaining integration questions: what superviseTransitions() does (it could cancel or retire loads, or touch stall handling), whether autopilotHeldWeightBytes() is cheap and actor-safe when called from the actor, and how resliceGateGeneration is consumed. None is a demonstrated security issue.
